## Personality

Eliza Andrews is a naturally grim and pessimistic individual whose gloomy outlook is frequently noted by others. Despite her dark disposition, she is deeply fond of her husband.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P60](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0060), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P24](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0024), [v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P64](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0064), [v2 XXII Odds and Ends P12](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0012)_

## History

Eliza Andrews was a dour woman who lived in a little brown house nestled in a sunny corner of Mark Andrew's beech woods with her optimistic sister, Catherine. During a visit from [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md), who were canvassing the area for the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village Improvement Society's hall painting fund, Eliza was approached for a contribution. She and her sister dealt with the young women as they successfully secured subscriptions for their cause.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P2](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0002), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P6](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0006), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P11](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0011), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P13](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0013), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), +142 more_

## Quotes

> "I don’t see the necessity. We didn’t gad about to halls and places when we were young, Catherine Andrews. This world is getting worse every day."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P18](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0018)

> "Doctors always talk like that just to keep people cheered up. I wouldn’t have much hope if I was her. It’s best to be prepared for the worst."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P27](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0027)

> “You think!” Miss Eliza’s voice expressed the utmost contempt. “It doesn’t signify what you think, Catherine Andrews. Facts is facts.”
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P20](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0020)

> "There isn’t any bright side."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P22](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0022)
